## phenix vm capture

Modify network packet captures for one or more VMs

### Synopsis

```text
Modify network packet captures for a VM

  Used to modify the network packet captures for virtual machines in a running
  experiment; see command help for start and stop for additional arguments.
```


## phenix vm capture stop

Stop packet captures for the specified VM

### Synopsis

```text
Stop packet captures for the specified VM

  If an interface name or index is provided, only the packet capture running
  on that interface is stopped, leaving any other running captures for the VM
  untouched. Otherwise, all packet captures for the VM are stopped.
```

```text
phenix vm capture stop <experiment name> <vm name> [iface name/index] [flags]
```

### Options

```text
  -h, --help   help for stop
```

### SEE ALSO

* [phenix vm capture](vm.md#phenix-vm-capture) - Modify network packet captures for one or more VMs

## phenix vm capture stream

Write a running packet capture to stdout as it is captured

### Synopsis

```text
Write a running packet capture to stdout as it is captured

  Writes the capture as a pcap stream: every packet captured so far (or, with
  --from-now, none of them), then each packet as it is captured, until the
  capture stops or the command is interrupted. Pipe it into Wireshark to
  watch it live:

    phenix vm capture stream <exp> <vm> <iface> | wireshark -k -i -
```

```text
phenix vm capture stream <experiment name> <vm name> <iface name/index> [flags]
```

### Options

```text
      --from-now        Skip the packets captured before the command started
  -h, --help            help for stream
  -o, --output string   Write the capture to this file instead of stdout
```

### SEE ALSO

* [phenix vm capture](vm.md#phenix-vm-capture) - Modify network packet captures for one or more VMs

## phenix vm info

Table of virtual machine(s)

### Synopsis

```text
Table of VM(s)

  Used to display a table of virtual machine(s) for a specific experiment;
  VM name is optional, when included will display only that VM.

  Filter the output by repeating --filter with a COLUMN=VALUE expression.
  Multiple filters are combined with AND semantics. Column names and values
  are case-insensitive. Supported columns are HOST, NAME, RUNNING, DISK,
  INTERFACES, UPTIME, MEMORY, VCPUS, OS_TYPE, and TAPS. DISK values may be
  full paths, filenames, or filenames without extensions. For example:

    phenix vm info my-experiment --filter RUNNING=true
    phenix vm info my-experiment --filter RUNNING=true --filter OS_TYPE=linux
    phenix vm info my-experiment --filter DISK=jammy
```

```text
phenix vm info <experiment name> [vm name] [flags]
```

### Options

```text
  -f, --filter stringArray   Filter output by column value (COLUMN=VALUE); may be repeated
  -h, --help                 help for info
  -l, --label stringArray    Label to filter VMs (supports glob patterns); use 'all' to select every VM
  -t, --taps                 Include tap interface names
```

### SEE ALSO

* [phenix vm](vm.md) - Virtual machine management

### Synopsis

## phenix vm mount

Mount a VM's filesystem on the headnode

### Synopsis

```text
Mount a VM's filesystem on the headnode

  Mount the filesystem of a running virtual machine to a directory on the
  headnode. By default, the mount path will be <mount-dir>/<experiment
  name>/<vm name> (see the --mount-dir root flag / PHENIX_MOUNT_DIR
  environment variable). An optional host path can be specified to mount to a
  custom location instead.
```

```text
phenix vm mount <experiment name> <vm name> [host path] [flags]
```

### Options

```text
  -h, --help   help for mount
```

### SEE ALSO

* [phenix vm](vm.md) - Virtual machine management

## phenix vm redeploy

Redeploy running experiment VM(s)

### Synopsis

```text
Redeploy running experiment VM(s)

  Used to redeploy running virtual machine(s) for a specific experiment; several redeploy
  values can be modified
```

```text
phenix vm redeploy <experiment name> [vm name] [flags]
```

### Options

```text
  -c, --cpu int             Number of VM CPUs (1-8 is valid) (default 1)
  -d, --disk string         VM backing disk image
  -h, --help                help for redeploy
  -l, --label stringArray   Label to filter VMs (supports glob patterns); use 'all' to select every VM
  -m, --mem int             Amount of memory in megabytes (512, 1024, 2048, 3072, 4096, 8192, 12288, 16384 are valid) (default 512)
  -p, --partition int       Partition of disk to inject files into (only used if disk option is specified) (default 1)
  -r, --replicate-injects   Recreate disk snapshot and VM injections
```

### SEE ALSO

* [phenix vm](vm.md) - Virtual machine management

## phenix vm set

Set configuration value(s) for VM(s)

### Synopsis

```text
Set configuration value(s) for VM(s)

  Used to set one or more configuration values for virtual machine(s) in an
  experiment. Only flags that are explicitly provided will be applied. While
  an experiment is running, only labels can be updated via this command (use
  'phenix vm net' to modify interface VLAN connections on a running
  experiment).
```

```text
phenix vm set <experiment name> [vm name] [flags]
```

### Options

```text
      --append-labels               Append the provided labels to the VM's existing labels instead of replacing the labels
  -c, --cpu int                     Number of VM CPUs (1-8 is valid)
  -d, --disk string                 VM backing disk image file
      --do-not-boot                 Set the do-not-boot flag for the VM
  -h, --help                        help for set
  -l, --label stringArray           Label to filter VMs (supports glob patterns); use 'all' to select every VM
  -L, --label-changes stringArray   VM label(s) to add or edit in key=value form (may be repeated)
  -m, --mem int                     Amount of memory in megabytes (512, 1024, 2048, 3072, 4096, 8192, 12288, 16384 are valid)
  -p, --partition int               Partition of disk to inject files into
      --snapshot                    Set the snapshot (non-persistent) flag for the VM
```

### SEE ALSO

* [phenix vm](vm.md) - Virtual machine management
